newsitem.title: USA: Continued fair skies for Brazil coffee belt - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Continued fair skies for Brazil coffee belt - WSC.

text.p: A strong ridge of high pressure is expected to continue to dominate Brazil's coffee belt promoting fair skies and mild temperatures, Weather Services Corp said in an update on Tuesday.

Colder air building into Argentina in the next few days is expected to pass off to the south of the coffee belt over the coming weekend bringing with it a possibility of cooler temperatures, but no damaging cold, according to WSC.
Mostly fair skies were observed in main growing areas of the belt this morning. Low temperatures ranged from 50-61 F (10-16 C). Some higher elevations reported cooler conditions.

The outlook calls for fair to partly cloudy skies through Thursday. Lows will be in the 50's to low 60's F (low to middle teens C). There is a chance of a few showers and thunderstorms developing on Friday. Some cooler conditions are still expected in higher elevations, although there is no sign of damaging cold, WSC said. ((Eileen Houlihan, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
